thought.text:
I have enough understanding of the bug. Let me implement the fix directly in `lookup_allowed`.

The issue: the concrete-inheritance shortcut at lines 467-470 skips appending a part when the field is the target of the previous relation's `target_fields`. This incorrectly triggers for a OneToOneField that is a primary key (not a parent link). The fix is to only apply the shortcut when the field is actually a parent link.

action.old_str:
# It is allowed to filter on values that would be found from local
            # model anyways. For example, if you filter on employee__department__id,
            # then the id value would be found already from employee__department_id.
            if not prev_field or (
                prev_field.is_relation
                and field not in prev_field.path_infos[-1].target_fields
            ):
                relation_parts.append(part)
action.new_str:
# It is allowed to filter on values that would be found from local
            # model anyways. For example, if you filter on employee__department__id,
            # then the id value would be found already from employee__department_id.
            if not prev_field or (
                prev_field.is_relation
                and field not in prev_field.path_infos[-1].target_fields
            ):
                relation_parts.append(part)
            if not getattr(field, "path_infos", None):
                # This is not a relational field, so further parts
                # must be transforms.
                break
            prev_field = field
            model = field.path_infos[-1].to_opts.model
